latest_release.name: Sure v0.7.6 — Clearer spending, smarter rules, and better backups
latest_release.body: With this monthly release (we haven't missed that cadence in more than a year!) Sure now helps you understand what changed in your spending and see your loans in greater detail. From the balance remaining to how each payment divides between principal, interest and insurance. It also brings more control over transaction categorization, improvements to Bills, and expanded backup and restore tools. ## See what's different in your spending The new [**Spending vs normal**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/4002) visualization compares your spending with your own history. A category treemap shows where your money went, while a ranked list highlights what increased or decreased. Open a category to explore the transactions behind the change. Enable preview features to try it! 🚀 *See where your money went—and which categories changed most compared with your usual spending.* ## Get a clearer picture of your loans [**Loan accounts**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/3474) now go beyond a remaining balance. See your loan graphically alongside the original repayment schedule and a projection from today, with a breakdown of principal and interest over the life of the loan. The expanded overview brings together your interest rate, monthly payment, term, insurance costs and projected payoff date. Explore the [**repayment schedule**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/3473) payment by payment; for adjustable-rate loans, recorded rate changes are reflected in the schedule. *Follow your mortgage from today's balance to projected payoff, with principal, interest and repayment details in one place.* ## Control over categorization, and more! Test the token-free [**Bayes classifier**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/4310) against your own history, inspect its results, and tune its settings. Merchant matching and category classification now participate in the ordered rules list. Drag rules to choose their order, use [**Stop processing**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/4013) for exceptions, and split recurring transactions by amount or percentage. Hide dashboard widgets you do not need, drag accounts into your preferred order, and filter account activity by category, tag, merchant or transaction type. Amount fields support calculator expressions and comma decimals. The Flutter mobile app gains a read-only [**Budgets**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/4426) screen with month navigation, category progress, rollover amounts and transaction drill-down. The expanded [**backup tooling**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/3909) covers the database, local uploads, configuration and version information, with restore and rollback workflows, scheduled backups and optional off-site copies. It builds on the database-only backup sidecar from 0.7.5. Uploads stored in external object storage are not included and need their own backup. Backup folders contain configuration secrets and must be kept private. ## Product-improvement monitoring ⚠️ We added monitoring to help improve features such as the new Sankey chart and to understand how they are used. Self-hosters can turn off this anonymous product-improvement monitoring by setting `POSTHOG_FEEDBACK_ENABLED=false` in the environment. ⚠️ ## Plus ... - [**Goals:**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/3974) fund a goal across currencies, with original and converted amounts and explicit warnings when exchange rates are missing. - [**Bills**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/4098) **and** [**cards:**](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/4270) clearer Bills drawers, payment flows and overdue states; a credit-card statement-cycle overview shows t

# Sure: The personal finance app for everyone Get involved: [Discord](https://discord.gg/36ZGBsxYEK) • [Website](https://sure.am) • [Issues](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues) > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository is a community fork of the now-abandoned Maybe Finance project.
> Learn more in their [final release](https://github.com/maybe-finance/maybe/releases/tag/v0.6.0) doc. ## Backstory The [Maybe Finance](https://github.com/maybe-finance/maybe) (archived/abandoned repo) team spent most of 2021–2022 building a full-featured personal finance and wealth management app. It even included an “Ask an Advisor” feature that connected users with a real CFP/CFA — all included with your subscription. The business end of things didn't work out, and so they stopped developing the app in mid-2023. After spending nearly $1 million on development (employees, contractors, data providers, infra, etc.), the team open-sourced the app. Their goal was to let users self-host it for free — and eventually launch a hosted version for a small fee. They actually did launch that hosted version … briefly. That also didn’t work out — at least not as a sustainable B2C business — so now here we are: hosting a community-maintained fork to keep the codebase alive and see where this can go next.
